, at the present, the best solution for wrapping relational databases to NoSQL ones is the one that is based on a middleware layer, which provides a SQL interface and a data model that can be mapped to the target NoSQL database, and also supports a large subset of the SQL language.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of open problems and challenges for the relational to NoSQL database wrapping solutions.
we have provided a survey that presents and discusses a wide range of relational to NoSQL wrapping approaches.

the approaches surveyed in this work can be organized in three groups: 1) those that provide an interface for relational data manipulation in the cloud; 2) those that provide a query interface that allows the execution of queries over data stored in NoSQL database; and 3) those that provide support to a subset of SQL operators and/or target a particular NoSQL database.

the most relevant open issues are: the definition and manipulation support of complex data structures, the integration of NoSQL database management features (such as sharding, replication and load balancing), and the support of SQL operations.
there is a lack of a general solution for the data wrapping of relational to NoSQL databases.
the choice of a wrapping solution should consider not only the target NoSQL database, but also the relational application to be wrapped.
